# Security Hunter Ledger

One line per entry, newest last.

- 2026-09-22 | FIXED | frontend | Dependency-graph tooltips (graph.js) interpolated an agent's `model` and `network` hostname-allow-list fields into `innerHTML` unescaped — neither is HTML-format-validated by AgentDefinition (parse_model only checks a "claude-" prefix, parse_network only checks "list of strings without *"), so a crafted definition executes script in the operator's browser on hover | frontend/trionyx_ui/static/js/graph.js, frontend/trionyx_ui/static/js/graph_safety.js
- 2026-09-22 | DOWNGRADED | frontend | `session_page`'s `page_path` (workspace/pages/<commit>/<path:page_path>) only extension-checks the final path segment; a `../` prefix survives to the gateway's `/pages/:commit/*` proxy and, after httpx's base_url dot-segment normalization, could retarget the request at an unrelated gateway route ending in .html/.htm. Low severity here (no matching gateway route is known to leak anything sensitive, and this needs a human to check what `/pages/:commit/*` actually resolves against on the gateway side — that's repo-store/gateway-http territory, not frontend) but worth a second look. | frontend/trionyx_ui/views/chat.py
- 2026-09-22 | DOWNGRADED | frontend | `chat.js`'s 'page' SSE event builds `pageUrl` as `` `/workspace/pages/${encodeURIComponent(data.commit)}/${data.path}` `` without encoding `data.path` (an agent-controlled field). A `../` sequence in `data.path` lets a compromised/prompt-injected agent redirect the "open in new tab" link and the sandboxed page-card iframe's `src` to an arbitrary same-origin dashboard URL. HTML-injection itself is prevented (the value only reaches attribute context via the existing `escapeAttr`), and the frontend has no auth today so the practical impact is limited, but it breaks the intended `/workspace/pages/<commit>/` proxy boundary and is worth hardening (encodeURIComponent each path segment) if the frontend ever gains auth or multi-operator use. | frontend/trionyx_ui/static/js/chat.js
